topics.name: Prompt Patterns
topics.description: MessagesPlaceholder, partial variables, single-variable input and few-shot chat prompts.
notes: - ChatPromptTemplate 的 messages 可以是 (type, template) 二元组、BaseMessage、BaseMessagePromptTemplate，或字符串（等价于 human 消息）。
- MessagesPlaceholder 用来插入一整段消息列表，例如对话历史。
- 默认 optional=False：必须传入同名参数（空列表也可以），否则报 KeyError。
- optional=True 时可以省略该参数；("placeholder", "{conversation}") 是等价的简写。
- partial_variables 或 .partial(...) 可以预先填入部分变量，调用时不必每次再传。
- 模板只有一个输入变量时，可以直接 invoke 一个非 dict 的值，它会被注入到该变量的位置。
- FewShotChatMessagePromptTemplate 生成的消息列表由前缀消息、示例消息、后缀消息组成。
- 示例可以是固定列表，也可以根据输入动态选择。
- 角色、语气和规则等长期指令应放在 SystemMessage 中。

topics.name: with_structured_output Methods
topics.description: Schema types, method options and include_raw for model-level structured output.
notes: - Pydantic 功能最全（字段校验、描述、嵌套），并提供自动校验。
- TypedDict 更简单，适合不需要运行时校验的场景；TypedDict 与 JSON Schema 需要手动校验。
- 'json_schema'：使用服务商专门提供的结构化输出能力。
- 'function_calling'：通过强制一次符合 schema 的 tool call 得到结构化输出。
- 'json_mode'：json_schema 的前身，保证输出合法 JSON，但 schema 必须写在提示词里。
- 具体支持哪些 method 取决于服务商的集成页面。
res = structured.invoke("Provide details about the movie Inception")
- raw 消息中包含 token 数等响应元数据。

topics.name: Agent response_format
topics.description: create_agent response_format, ProviderStrategy, ToolStrategy and error handling.
notes: - 结构化结果保存在 agent 最终状态的 structured_response 键中。
- 直接传 schema 类型时：模型和服务商支持原生结构化输出则用 ProviderStrategy，否则用 ToolStrategy。
- JSON Schema 字典不会被自动识别，必须显式包装成 ProviderStrategy 或 ToolStrategy。
- ProviderStrategy 使用服务商原生能力，由服务商强制 schema；strict 参数需要 langchain>=1.2，默认 None（关闭）。
- Pydantic 返回校验后的实例；dataclass、TypedDict、JSON Schema 返回 dict。
- ToolStrategy 通过 tool calling 实现，支持 Union 类型；handle_errors 默认 True，校验失败时把错误反馈给模型重试。
- handle_errors 可以是 bool、str、异常类型、异常类型元组、回调函数；False 表示不重试，直接抛出异常。
- prompt | model | parser 这样的链没有内置的解析重试，handle_errors 只作用于 create_agent。
- 可以改用 with_structured_output，或用 langchain-classic 的 OutputFixingParser 包装 parser。

topics.name: Runnable Composition
notes: - RunnableParallel 把同一个输入同时交给多个 Runnable，返回以键名为索引的 dict。
- 在序列里写 dict 字面量，会被自动转换成 RunnableParallel。
- RunnablePassthrough 原样传递输入；.assign(...) 在保留输入 dict 的同时增加新键。
- RunnableLambda 把 Python 可调用对象变成 Runnable，适合不需要流式的代码；
需要按 chunk 处理流时应使用 RunnableGenerator。
- RunnableLambda 若返回 Runnable，该 Runnable 会被继续执行（或流式执行）。
- batch() 在客户端并行处理多个独立请求，不同于服务商自己的 Batch API。
- config={"max_concurrency": 5} 可限制并行调用数量。
- batch_as_completed() 每个结果完成就返回，顺序可能乱，结果带有输入下标。
- stream() 返回 AIMessageChunk，chunk 可以用 + 累加成完整消息。

questions.title: A template contains MessagesPlaceholder("history") with the default settings. What must you do when invoking it?

options.text: Nothing; the placeholder is skipped automatically when the key is missing
Pass a list of messages under "history", even if it is an empty list
Pass a single string under "history"
Set n_messages on the template first

questions.explanation: With the default optional=False the named argument must be supplied, otherwise a KeyError is raised. Only optional=True lets you omit it.

questions.title: How many messages does value.messages contain?

options.text: 3, because the placeholder counts as one message
4: the system message, the two history messages and the human question
2, because history replaces the system message
5, because each history entry adds two messages

questions.explanation: The placeholder is expanded in place into the messages it receives. Here that gives system, human, ai and the final human message.

questions.title: In ChatPromptTemplate, what does the entry ("placeholder", "{conversation}") mean?

options.text: A required string variable named conversation
A partial variable that is filled once at construction time
An optional list of messages passed under the "conversation" key
A system message that contains the word conversation

questions.explanation: It is shorthand for MessagesPlaceholder(variable_name="conversation", optional=True). A plain string variable would use a human or system tuple instead.

questions.title: Which method pre-fills the lang variable so that invoke only needs question?
questions.codeSnippet:
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    ("system", "Answer in {lang}."),
    ("human", "{question}"),
]).______(lang="French")
prompt.invoke({"question": "What is LCEL?"})

options.text: append
save
partial
bind

questions.explanation: partial() fills some template variables up front, matching the partial_variables concept. append() adds a message to the template and save() writes it to disk.

questions.title: What is the content of the last message in value.messages?
questions.codeSnippet:
template = ChatPromptTemplate([
    ("system", "You are a helpful AI bot. Your name is Carl."),
    ("human", "{user_input}"),
])
value = template.invoke("Hello, there!")
print(value.messages[-1].content)

options.text: A TypeError is raised because invoke needs a dict
"{user_input}"
"Hello, there!"
"You are a helpful AI bot. Your name is Carl."

questions.explanation: With only one input variable, a non-dict argument is injected into that variable. So invoke("Hello, there!") is equivalent to passing {"user_input": "Hello, there!"}.

questions.title: Which of these can be used as an entry in the messages list of ChatPromptTemplate?

options.text: A 2-tuple such as ("human", "{user_input}")
A plain string such as "{user_input}", shorthand for a human message
A BaseMessagePromptTemplate such as MessagesPlaceholder
A bare integer that selects a stored message by index

questions.explanation: The documented message representations include templates, BaseMessage objects, (type, template) tuples and strings. An integer index is not a supported form.

questions.title: What structure does FewShotChatMessagePromptTemplate produce?

options.text: A single string that joins all examples
A fine-tuned model checkpoint
A list of messages made of prefix, example and suffix messages
Only the example messages, without any prefix or suffix

questions.explanation: It builds a conversation in which example human/AI turns sit between the prefix and suffix messages. It does not train anything.

questions.title: Which schema type does the Models guide say offers the richest feature set for with_structured_output (validation, descriptions, nested structures)?

options.text: TypedDict
A JSON Schema dictionary
A plain Python dict of field names
Pydantic models

questions.explanation: Pydantic models provide field validation, descriptions and nested structures. TypedDict is a simpler alternative without runtime validation.

questions.title: The model returns valid data for the Movie schema. What does this print?
questions.codeSnippet:
structured = model.with_structured_output(Movie, include_raw=True)
res = structured.invoke("Provide details about the movie Inception")
print(res["parsing_error"])

options.text: An empty string
None
False
A KeyError, because the result is a Movie object

questions.explanation: With include_raw=True the result is a dict with raw, parsed and parsing_error keys. When parsing succeeds, parsing_error is None.

questions.title: Which statements about schema types for with_structured_output are correct?

options.text: Pydantic models give automatic validation
TypedDict and JSON Schema require manual validation
A TypedDict schema returns a Pydantic instance
A JSON Schema dict can be passed together with method="json_schema"

questions.explanation: The docs state Pydantic validates automatically while TypedDict and JSON Schema need manual validation. A TypedDict schema yields a plain dict, not a Pydantic object.

questions.title: What does method="function_calling" do in with_structured_output?

options.text: It derives structured output by forcing a tool call that follows the given schema
It uses the provider's dedicated structured output feature
It only produces valid JSON and expects the schema to be described in the prompt
It executes your Python functions to build the answer

questions.explanation: function_calling forces a tool call matching the schema. Option B describes json_schema and option C describes json_mode.

questions.title: Which statement about method="json_mode" is correct?

options.text: It generates valid JSON, but the schema has to be described in the prompt
It enforces the schema server-side through the provider's schema feature
It works by forcing a tool call and needs no prompt instructions
It returns the raw AIMessage together with the parsed output

questions.explanation: json_mode is a precursor to json_schema offered by some providers: valid JSON is generated but the schema must be described in the prompt. Returning the raw message is the job of include_raw.

questions.title: Fill in the blank so that the provider's dedicated structured output feature is used with a JSON Schema dict.
questions.codeSnippet:
model_with_structure = model.with_structured_output(
    json_schema,
    method="______",
)
response = model_with_structure.invoke("Provide details about the movie Inception")

options.text: function_calling
json_mode
json_schema
pydantic

questions.explanation: 'json_schema' uses the provider's dedicated structured output feature, as in the JSON Schema example in the docs. 'pydantic' is not a method value.

questions.title: You need token counts for a with_structured_output call. How do you get them next to the parsed result?

options.text: Pass include_raw=True and read the metadata on the raw AIMessage
Read them from the Pydantic object, which always has a usage field
Switch to method="json_mode", which adds token counts
Call the model twice, once with and once without a schema

questions.explanation: include_raw=True returns the raw AIMessage along with the parsed output, so response metadata such as token counts stays accessible. The parsed schema object only holds your own fields.

questions.title: With create_agent and response_format, where is the structured result found?

options.text: In the structured_response key of the agent's final state
In result["parsed"]
In the content of the first message
In a file next to the script

questions.explanation: The structured response is captured, validated and returned under structured_response. The parsed key belongs to with_structured_output(include_raw=True) instead.

questions.title: You pass a Pydantic class directly as response_format to create_agent. Which strategy does LangChain choose?

options.text: Always ToolStrategy
ProviderStrategy if the model and provider support native structured output, otherwise ToolStrategy
Always ProviderStrategy
No strategy; the schema is only added to the system prompt

questions.explanation: A schema type triggers automatic selection based on model capabilities. Native support gives ProviderStrategy, everything else falls back to ToolStrategy.

questions.title: The schema below is a JSON Schema dict, but the agent does not use it as intended. What is the fix?
questions.codeSnippet:
schema = {
    "title": "ContactInfo",
    "description": "Contact information.",
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}},
    "required": ["name"],
}
agent = create_agent(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[],
    response_format=schema,
)

options.text: Remove the title key
Pass strict=True to create_agent
Convert the dict to a string with json.dumps
Wrap it, for example response_format=ProviderStrategy(schema)

questions.explanation: JSON Schema dictionaries are not auto-detected when passed directly to response_format. They must be wrapped in an explicit ProviderStrategy or ToolStrategy.

questions.title: What type is result["structured_response"]?
questions.codeSnippet:
@dataclass
class ContactInfo:
    name: str
    email: str

agent = create_agent(model="gpt-5.5", tools=[], response_format=ContactInfo)
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "John Doe, john@example.com"}]})
print(type(result["structured_response"]).__name__)

options.text: ContactInfo
BaseModel
AIMessage
dict

questions.explanation: Per the docs, dataclass schemas return a dict, while only Pydantic models return a validated instance of the class.

questions.title: During structured output generation a RuntimeError is raised. What happens with this configuration?
questions.codeSnippet:
response_format = ToolStrategy(
    schema=ProductRating,
    handle_errors=(ValueError, TypeError),
)
agent = create_agent(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[],
    response_format=response_format,
)

options.text: The agent retries using the default error message
The error is swallowed and structured_response is None
The RuntimeError is raised, because only the listed exception types trigger a retry
The tuple is invalid and fails when the agent is created

questions.explanation: A tuple of exception types makes the agent retry only for those types, and any other exception is raised. Retrying on every error is what handle_errors=True does.

questions.title: Which are documented ways to deal with malformed model output in a chain like prompt | model | parser?

options.text: Bind the schema with model.with_structured_output
Wrap the parser in OutputFixingParser from langchain-classic
Rely on ToolStrategy handle_errors, which retries automatically inside any pipe chain
Rely on the chain's built-in parsing retry

questions.explanation: Chains built with the pipe operator have no built-in retry for parsing failures, and handle_errors only applies to create_agent. Use native structured output or OutputFixingParser instead.

questions.title: What is true about the strict parameter of ProviderStrategy?

options.text: It defaults to True and works with every provider
It makes ToolStrategy skip validation
It defaults to None (disabled), is supported by some providers such as OpenAI and xAI, and requires langchain>=1.2
It only affects Pydantic schemas and is ignored for JSON Schema

questions.explanation: strict is an optional boolean for strict schema adherence that defaults to None. Only some providers support it and it needs langchain>=1.2.

questions.title: Which values are accepted for the handle_errors parameter of ToolStrategy?

options.text: A string, used as a fixed retry message
A tuple of exception types
A callable that takes the exception and returns a message string
A dict mapping exception names to retry counts

questions.explanation: The docs list bool, str, an exception type, a tuple of exception types and a Callable[[Exception], str]. A dict of retry counts is not supported.

questions.title: What does RunnableParallel do with its input?

options.text: It splits the input into equal parts, one per branch
It runs the branches one after another, each using the previous output
It gives the same input to every branch, runs them concurrently and returns a mapping of their outputs
It runs only the first branch that succeeds

questions.explanation: RunnableParallel provides the same input to each Runnable and returns their outputs in a dict. Sequential chaining is the job of RunnableSequence.

questions.title: What does sequence.invoke(1) return?
questions.codeSnippet:
runnable_1 = RunnableLambda(lambda x: x + 1)
runnable_2 = RunnableLambda(lambda x: x * 2)
runnable_3 = RunnableLambda(lambda x: x * 3)

sequence = runnable_1 | {
    "mul_two": runnable_2,
    "mul_three": runnable_3,
}
print(sequence.invoke(1))

options.text: {'mul_two': 4, 'mul_three': 6}
{'mul_two': 2, 'mul_three': 3}
A TypeError, because a dict cannot be piped

questions.explanation: The dict literal is coerced into a RunnableParallel. Both branches receive 2 (the output of the first step) and return 4 and 6.

questions.title: What does this chain print?

options.text: {'total_chars': 20}
{'llm1': 'completion', 'llm2': 'completion', 'total_chars': 20}
{'llm1': 'completion', 'llm2': 'completion', 'total_chars': 10}
hello

questions.explanation: assign() keeps the incoming dict and adds the new key. total_chars is the length of 'completioncompletion', which is 20, and a bare assign does not drop llm1 or llm2.

questions.title: A custom step must operate on chunks of a stream and yield chunks. Which class does the RunnableLambda reference recommend instead of RunnableLambda?

options.text: RunnableParallel
RunnableGenerator
RunnablePassthrough
RunnableSequence

questions.explanation: RunnableLambda is best suited for code that does not need to support streaming. RunnableGenerator is the documented choice for transforming chunks of input into chunks of output.

questions.title: Which RunnableConfig key limits batch() to 5 parallel calls?

options.text: max_workers
batch_size
max_concurrency
recursion_limit

questions.explanation: max_concurrency controls the maximum number of parallel calls for batch() and batch_as_completed(). recursion_limit bounds chain depth, not parallelism.

questions.title: Which statements about model.batch() and model.batch_as_completed() are correct?

options.text: batch() parallelizes the calls on the client side
batch() calls the provider's own Batch API, such as OpenAI's
batch_as_completed() yields each result as it finishes, possibly out of order, with the input index
batch() requires the model to be in streaming mode

questions.explanation: batch() is client-side parallelism and is distinct from provider batch APIs. batch_as_completed() yields results as they complete, so each one carries its input index for reordering.
